skill.name: documentation-audit
skill.description: Audits documentation claims against the current codebase using structured extraction, verification, pattern expansion, and gap detection.
skill.summary: Verify documentation accuracy by checking claims against real codebase evidence.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, regex examples, and references to .env.example. Semantic review found one real risk: the skill suggests running target repository scripts to inspect CLI help, which can execute untrusted code. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: CLI verification can execute untrusted repository code.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer static inspection of argparse, click, Typer, or README usage text. Run target scripts only in a sandbox after user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Environment checks could be misread as permission to inspect real secret files.
remediation.suggestion: State that audits should use .env.example, schemas, and source defaults. Avoid reading real .env files unless the user explicitly approves.

remediation.issue: Command examples lack safety boundaries for untrusted projects.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to treat audited repositories as untrusted and to avoid executing project code during documentation checks.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Repository Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The CLI verification pattern recommends running a target project script with a help flag. In an untrusted repository, even help output can execute Python initialization or argument parsing side effects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is shown as a verification method and would execute code from the audited repository. The risk is contextual rather than malicious, but it is a real local code execution hazard.

content.value_statement: Documentation can drift after refactors, releases, and deleted files. This skill extracts claims, checks them against code, and produces an evidence-based audit report.
actual_capabilities: Extracts verifiable claims from user-facing documentation.
Checks file references, defaults, environment variables, CLI flags, and behavior claims.
Expands searches from false claims to find related documentation drift.
Compares documented scripts, services, config modules, and endpoints against repository inventory.
Generates an audit report with evidence, false claims, suggested fixes, and human-review items.
limitations: Behavior claims often need human review because code evidence may be indirect.
Results depend on repository access and the quality of available source files.
Pattern expansion can produce false positives that need triage.
The skill reports documentation issues but does not update files automatically.

use_cases.title: Release Documentation Gate
use_cases.description: Check user-facing docs before release and identify stale claims that could mislead users.

use_cases.title: Post-Refactor Docs Review
use_cases.description: Verify that renamed files, settings, services, and CLI options are reflected in documentation.

use_cases.title: Documentation Debt Triage
use_cases.description: Group false claims by pattern so teams can fix high-impact documentation drift first.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Use documentation-audit to check README.md against the current repository. List false claims, uncertain claims, and evidence for each result.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Selected Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use documentation-audit on README.md and docs/*.md. Focus on file references, configuration defaults, environment variables, CLI flags, and timing claims.

prompt_templates.title: Run Two-Pass Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use documentation-audit to extract claims from user-facing docs, verify them, then search for related patterns from every false claim. Produce an audit report.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use documentation-audit before release. Compare documented scripts, services, config values, and CLI options with the codebase. Include blockers and human-review items.

output_examples.output: The report identifies 42 claims, confirms 36, marks 4 false, and sends 2 behavior claims to human review.

output_examples.input: Check docs after a configuration refactor.
output_examples.output: Finds stale default values, unsupported environment variables, and missing script documentation with file and line evidence.

output_examples.input: Compare documented services with actual service files.
output_examples.output: Summarizes missing service references, renamed timers, and suggested documentation fixes for maintainers.

best_practices: Audit user-facing docs first and exclude plans or historical notes unless requested.
Keep file and line evidence beside every true, false, and uncertain verdict.
Run pattern expansion after the first false claims are grouped.
anti_patterns: Treating plausible prose as verified without checking source evidence.
Running target project scripts just to inspect help text outside a sandbox.
Mixing historical plans with current user documentation in the same audit.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits documentation claims about files, settings, environment variables, CLI flags, services, timers, and behavior.

faq.question: Does it edit documentation?
faq.answer: No. It creates an audit report with evidence and suggested fixes for maintainers.

faq.question: Can it verify behavior claims?
faq.answer: It can collect supporting evidence, but behavior claims often need human review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prefer static checks and avoid executing project code unless it is sandboxed and approved.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a documentation audit report with counts, false claims, evidence, patterns, and human-review items.
